qs.q: A 45-year-old male living in coastal East Africa presents with massive scrotal swelling, bilateral lower limb elephantiasis, and milky urine. Which underlying mechanism best describes the primary pathophysiology of his condition?
o: Low-output lymphatic failure from worm-induced obstruction
High-output capillary filtration exceeding normal lymph capacity
Primary lymphatic aplasia due to mid-gestational venous defect
Hyperplasia of lymphatic vessels with intrinsic valve failure
qs.e: Lymphoedema caused by filariasis represents low-output lymphatic failure due to adult worms obstructing the lymphatics. High-output failure and primary aplasia represent different etiologies not matching this endemic parasitic infection.
